requirements: Verify whole bundle bytes and every file hash before using templates.
Extract only the listed paths into scratch outside the app; never overwrite an app from this bundle.
The native builder prepares app-bound paths, import adaptations, current SDK/runtime entry and source diffs for review.
Preserve login, existing features, governance artifacts and native AI Controls.
Use actual independent evidence for the snapshot; no fixture, synthetic status or invented completed stages.
Snapshot source, role checks and exact app binding stay server-only. Preserve the native resume and approved update writer handoff.
Status grant provisioning, owner secure Secret entry and beta service deployment are separate dependencies.
Do not claim live readiness until installation, exact readback, real role checks, persistence and governance behavior pass.

# Base44 owner/admin BOS status backend

State: local implementation for the separately approved owner/admin BOS page.
Not installed in Base44, published as a companion, or enabled by this template.

## Installation boundary

Native Base44 installs `entry.ts`, `handler.js` and `auth.js` together inside its
configured backend-function directory, under an exact app-surface source plan.
Use the target's independently observed resource layout; do not initialize a new
app or change its login, roles or subscription model. The template defaults to
disabled and has no app ID, URL, credential or grant.

The reviewed plan must fill these `entry.ts` literals:

- `enabled: true` only after the separate backend function is approved;
- `project_ref`: the exact authenticated `base44:<24-hex-app-id>`;
- `status_url`: the exact approved public Cloud BOS HTTPS audience ending in
  `/mcp/app-status`, without query, fragment, port or user information.

Enabling this function does not enable the Worker or register status access.
The Cloud BOS deployment, access-plan approval and fingerprint registration
remain separate. Retain the app's current SDK version in its exact source plan,
verify it against this adapter, and test the deployed runtime before claiming
customer readiness. This draft entry uses Base44's documented default-export
handler and request-time `base44:runtime` Secrets API.

## Authorization and storage

The app SDK invokes this backend with its existing signed-in user's session.
`auth.js` configures a user-scoped SDK client for the exact reviewed app and the
official production Base44 API. Caller-supplied app/API/service-role headers
cannot retarget it. It calls `auth.me()` for each request and requires an
identified user with the actual `admin` role before reading any Secret or
calling Cloud BOS. Display labels, client tier fields and app-owner claims are
not role authority. Verify the actual owner/admin role mapping in the live app.

Only the two per-app Secrets `BOS_APP_STATUS_A` and `BOS_APP_STATUS_B` are read.
Reads occur during an authorized request. This backend writes no source,
entities, secrets, credentials, browser storage, logs, decisions or approvals.
It returns no raw credentials and performs no service-role operation.

## Page-facing API

Call the installed function through the existing Base44 SDK. The frontend
adapter must unwrap the SDK response according to the target's observed SDK
version; do not treat an Axios wrapper as the JSON status payload.

| JSON request | Successful result |
|---|---|
| `{"action":"STATUS"}` | `STATUS_READ`, exact project, working slot, allowlisted connection metadata |
| `{"action":"FINGERPRINT","slot":"A"}` | `SECRET_FINGERPRINT_READY`, exact project/slot, SHA-256 and `grants_access:false` |
| `{"action":"FINGERPRINT","slot":"B"}` | Same fingerprint-only response for the other slot |

Unknown actions, arbitrary Secret names, client credentials, app IDs, URLs,
tier fields and additional request properties are rejected. Fingerprinting
proves only what is saved in that slot. It does not approve or activate access.

The page must display the returned `observed_at` separately from
`governance_evidence.last_verified_at`. The latter is a dated stored record;
`source_reread_this_request` stays false. A successful refresh is not a new
source scan, completed onboarding, build approval or paid entitlement grant.

Errors are closed, plain status codes: sign-in required, owner/admin required,
setup required, secret missing/invalid, access unavailable/restricted, rate
limited, or service unavailable. Do not convert them to connected or retain a
previous green status as current. No raw upstream error is relayed. All
responses use `no-store` and provide no browser CORS grant.

## Rotation and pauses

The backend tries A, then B only if A is absent, malformed or denied. Identical
slot values are not sent twice. It stops on rate limits, outages and redirects.
The old slot can therefore keep working while an unregistered candidate is
saved to the inactive slot. After the separately approved atomic BOS rotation,
the new slot succeeds. The current slot comes from a successful status response;
missing status is not evidence that either saved slot is safe to overwrite.

The page's remaining setup flow must prepare a random value in owner browser
memory, provide explicit Copy, guide secure owner entry, compare backend
fingerprints, and request the exact access plan through native Cloud BOS tools.
Never pass the raw value through chat or an MCP tool. Do not overwrite a working
slot merely because the other slot, a chat session or a local scratch file is
unavailable.

There is an eight-second request budget, including authentication, Secret reads,
both possible status attempts and response reading. It cancels downstream reads
and rejects late work. This is an I/O limit, not an access or approval expiry.
A response observation outside a one-minute clock-tolerance window is rejected
as stale; it does not revoke the credential or require a new approval. Old
governance evidence is preserved with its original date, not rewritten as new.

## Verification

`node scripts/test_base44_app_status_backend.mjs` covers authorization, exact
scope, response privacy, stored-evidence dates, rotation, revocation, downgrade,
timeouts and cancellation. It also composes this handler with the actual Cloud
BOS reader using synthetic database rows; it does not claim live D1 or Base44.

`node scripts/test_base44_app_status_sdk.mjs` additionally exercises the installed
Base44 SDK with a local HTTP interceptor and compiles the complete disabled
function. Set `BOS_BASE44_SDK_MODULE` only to an existing SDK module path if needed.
It sends no real network requests. Verified locally with SDK 0.8.41; the live
app's SDK/runtime, role mapping and saved Secret readback still need testing.

Official references checked 16 September 2026:

- https://docs.base44.com/developers/backend/resources/backend-functions/overview
- https://docs.base44.com/developers/references/sdk/docs/functions/createClient
- https://docs.base44.com/developers/references/sdk/docs/functions/createClientFromRequest

The owner/admin page, progress evidence writer, existing memory-card integration,
secure entry UI and native header/tour acceptance are still separate unfinished
work. This backend template cannot complete any of those steps by itself.

# Owner/admin BOS page

Source template for a separately reviewed Base44 app-surface plan. Publishing
this template does not install or update any connected app.

## Source and layout

`BosStatusPage.jsx` supplies the persistent full-page view, a navigation
connection indicator and the single floating BOS launcher. Reuse the existing
app shell and sign-in flow. Preserve the app's own title page and identity.
Only identified app users with the actual `admin` role see these components;
each backend independently enforces its current authorization. Client role
props are presentation only. Unmount on sign-out or an account change.

Wrap the existing app navigation and routed BOS page in one
`BosConnectionProvider` with the same identified `viewer`, exact `projectRef`
and stable `client`. Pass that viewer and project reference to
`BosConnectionIndicator`. The provider performs one status read shared by the
navigation and page; opening the page does not create a second status check.
Refresh updates both. Account, app or loader changes discard old results before
rendering; sign-out and ordinary-user access make no status request. A page used
alone can create its own provider, but a navigation indicator must use the shared
shell provider, not caller-supplied status props.

The five visible states are CONNECTED (explicitly labelled **Connected when
checked**, with its observation time), DISCONNECTED (setup missing or governance
detached), DEGRADED (service failure or governance drift), BLOCKED (access
restricted), and UNKNOWN_VISIBLE (loading, missing, malformed or cross-app
evidence). Elapsed time does not disconnect a binding or expire approval. A dated
observation remains dated; a subsequent refresh can establish a changed state.
Neither display is a continuous-monitoring or fresh-source-verification claim.

Use the existing canonical `BosMemoryCard` component, stylesheet and summary
reader from `plugins/cloudbos-public-plugin`. Adapt its relative import as part
of the exact source plan, preserving the reviewed component bytes otherwise.
Copy `public/assets/brand/bos-icon-192.png` into the app's approved public asset
path. Its SHA-256 is
`77f2cf444a95f8df56de6fcef3af17bb486186446156b1b2acedf8fc2be33632`.
It is the reviewed derivative of the owner-selected BOS character icon.

The cream, black, muted green and red style uses the existing icon with a
1960s-inspired serif masthead. Public links are fixed to the BOS website,
support page and tier comparison anchor. They contain no app identifiers or
tokens and grant no paid access. The page adds no checkout or product gating.

## Plan and price display

The current plan is the validated authenticated status response, with its check
time. Missing, denied or mismatched status shows **Not verified**, never a free
or paid default. An internal Creator admin profile is named but not sold.

`pricing-client.js` reads the public BOS website's fixed
`data/bos-beta-pricing.json` URL without cookies, app identifiers or a referrer.
The bounded response is validated before display. It supplies the approved AUD
list prices and billing periods, independently of the app's entitlement. No
cached local list is passed off as a successful current price read. A failed
read leaves a visible website link and prices-unavailable message. Refresh
status retries both reads. The four comparison cards link to the BOS website;
they do not take payment, assign a plan or send the app's context there.

The list is governed by `OS/COMMERCIAL/BOS_PRIVATE_BETA_PRICING_AUTHORITY.md`:
Standard A$0 ongoing, Plus A$39/month, Pro A$99/month, Enterprise custom/not yet
priced. Paid options remain invite-only beta and checkout is not live. Display
the inclusions/exclusions and attended delivery limitations. List prices are
not a user's invoice or proof of subscription. Price changes require the
canonical commercial decision and companion checks before publication.

## Backend integration

Create one stable `createStatusPageClient(base44)` from the app's existing SDK
client. The adapter calls the exact installed functions `bosAppStatus` and
`bosAppSnapshot`. It unwraps `response.data`, preserves bounded typed failures
and hides raw SDK diagnostics. It never sends an app ID, role or tier override.

`bosAppStatus` is the independently tested template in the parent directory.
`bosAppSnapshot` has a local backend and preparation template in `../snapshot/`.
Its native writer and live installation remain required integrations. The UI
calls its PROGRESS and MEMORY reads and displays unavailable while it is missing.
The MEMORY response uses the existing `BOS_APP_MEMORY_SUMMARY_V1` contract.
Do not ship the local fixture or a permanently frozen example as this backend.

The PROGRESS response is a selected summary of independently recorded checks:

```json
{
  "schema": "BOS_APP_ONBOARDING_SUMMARY_V1",
  "project_ref": "base44:<exact app id>",
  "source_revision": "<full 40-hex source revision read back>",
  "captured_at": "<actual source-review time>",
  "stages": [
    {"id":"connection","status":"UNKNOWN","recorded_at":null},
    {"id":"baseline","status":"UNKNOWN","recorded_at":null},
    {"id":"plan","status":"UNKNOWN","recorded_at":null},
    {"id":"governance","status":"UNKNOWN","recorded_at":null},
    {"id":"ai_controls","status":"UNKNOWN","recorded_at":null},
    {"id":"readiness","status":"UNKNOWN","recorded_at":null}
  ]
}
```

These six display groups summarize the existing onboarding contract:

| Group | Evidence required before VERIFIED |
|---|---|
| connection | Exact account MCP connection and enabled workspace skill readback |
| baseline | Exact app discovery, bounded health review with findings, accepted app baseline |
| plan | Exact app-bound setup plan and recorded owner decision |
| governance | Activation, independent artifact readback and currentness verification |
| ai_controls | Independently reopened native setting text matches the canonical pointer |
| readiness | Connection page/source/UI readback and the required native governance/onboarding acceptance checks |

Use WAITING for a known pending step, NEEDS_ATTENTION for an observed issue and
UNKNOWN for missing evidence. A VERIFIED record requires its observation date.
The trusted writer, never client request JSON, derives these fields from exact
app-bound evidence and stores them with the source revision and capture time.
It updates both summaries after accepted changes. A refresh never invents new
capture dates, approvals or checks. The displayed count measures recorded setup
checks, not product maturity, fresh health, paid access or release readiness.

## Key preparation and recovery

The setup panel starts with a fresh backend status read. It uses A only when
neither key is saved, or the other slot when the backend proves a working slot.
It then verifies the intended slot is empty before preparing a 32-byte CSPRNG
candidate. An occupied or unverified slot is never automatically overwritten.
Existing-key replacement remains a native, reviewed recovery action.

Raw candidates live only in a React ref, never page text, DOM inputs, browser
storage, URL parameters, logs, analytics or app source. Copy uses a separate
explicit click. The owner opens Base44's secure Set secrets form, pastes the
key there themselves and saves it. Setup instructions and review prompts use
separate copy buttons and contain no raw key. Clipboard denial remains visible.

Checking the saved key calls the owner-authorized fingerprint endpoint and
requires an exact match to the prepared candidate before saying it matches.
After that check, the raw candidate is discarded. Only the fingerprint enters
the native connection-plan review prompt. Copying that prompt does not approve
or apply anything. Current status comes from a subsequent real backend check.

After a reload or pause, Use an already saved key reads fingerprints from the
backend and prepares a review request. It does not claim recovery of the
original plaintext or an exact match to lost browser memory. BOS reads its
durable access record and recovers the appropriate pending plan or proposes
the required new one. Clearing local preparation affects only this tab's
unsaved candidate and display state, not saved Secrets or Cloud BOS access.

## Local verification

`node scripts/test_base44_status_page_model.mjs` tests display data boundaries,
progress honesty, credential generation/fingerprints and SDK argument scope.
`node scripts/render_base44_status_page_preview.mjs <absolute temp directory>`
builds the actual component and canonical icon with a clearly labelled local
fixture. Its clipboard and Secret writes are in-memory mocks, never system
clipboard or provider writes. Use computer control to test the rendered
scenarios, resize behavior, key mismatch/recovery, roles and stale responses.
Never include `scripts/fixtures/base44_status_page_preview.jsx` in an app plan.
The generated `responsive.html` harness tests the actual component at 320, 375
and 768 CSS pixels inside a frame. It does not claim physical-device testing.
The SDK adapter bounds client waits and discards aborted reads; it does not
claim to cancel a provider request when the SDK exposes no cancellation input.

Required live acceptance remains exact app plan approval, native installation,
source readback, actual owner/ordinary-user/signed-out behavior, saved records
and key recovery after reload, restriction/revocation, mobile layout and native
chat governance. Local fixtures cannot prove those live outcomes.

# Durable app snapshot adapter

Local source template for the separately approved `bosAppSnapshot` backend.
Nothing in this directory is installed in the live acceptance app yet.

The app's saved source files are the persistence layer. The backend imports
`reviewed-snapshot.json` into its server bundle and returns only the requested
PROGRESS or MEMORY projection after a fresh authenticated `admin` role check.
It reuses the exact-app, user-only SDK adapter in `../auth.js`. No service-role
credential, Cloud BOS key, new entity, public asset, browser storage or central
database is involved. No request can write observations or choose an app.

## Preparing real data

Use `scripts/prepare_base44_app_snapshot.mjs` during the existing native
builder's governed projection step. Its arguments are the exact app root,
review packet path, independently checked review packet SHA-256 and a new
output path outside the app. The command refuses dirty or changed source,
wrong revisions, missing or mismatched expected artifact hashes, unsupported
source paths and output overwrite. It reads eight lean governance artifacts,
plus the security baseline when declared by the reviewed hash list.

The review packet has schema `BOS_BASE44_SNAPSHOT_SOURCE_REVIEW_V1` and contains:

- Exact `project_ref` and `source_revision` independently read back.
- `artifact_sha256`: every required file's expected hash from the approved
  installed plan and its verified manifest, not hashes invented from the
  observed bytes merely to pass this check.
- `canonical_pointer_sha256`: the verified canonical public AI Controls
  payload hash, not an installation approval hash.
- `stages`: the six recorded setup groups with status, observation date and
  attributed evidence. Waiting or unknown steps have `recorded_at: null`.

Each VERIFIED or NEEDS_ATTENTION row requires `evidence.reference`, its exact
`sha256` and the actual `observer`. VERIFIED rows also require the corresponding
`EVIDENCE_KINDS` value in `model.js`. The AI Controls row requires independent
reopened UI readback and the exact pointer hash. A user saying Saved, a model
self-check or a historical manifest marker does not satisfy that condition.
The governance row requires independent artifact readback for the source
revision being summarized. Dates cannot be newer than the source capture.

Hash and schema checks validate consistency; they do not authenticate the
observer or prove an event occurred. The operator must independently inspect
the cited evidence before including it in the reviewed app-surface plan.
Do not turn a copied chat claim into a verified source record. Preserve Codex,
owner and BuildAI attribution accurately.

The preparer derives memory using the existing canonical memory-summary helper.
Only deliberately selected owner/admin text may be summarized. A selected
field is not a secret detector: private prompts, credentials and customer
records must not be inserted into display fields. Raw source and ledger
bodies never cross into the frontend response.

## Installation and updates

1. Independently inspect the complete generated JSON, recorded observations,
   source revision and output hash. Add these exact bytes and the backend
   files to the separate app-surface proposal. The preparer grants no approval.
2. After exact approval, the native Base44 builder installs the backend with
   the exact app binding and these reviewed bytes. Adapt imports for its
   function directory, including the existing memory helper and auth adapter.
   Keep the JSON in the backend function directory, never `src/` or `public/`.
3. Checkpoint and independently read back the installed files and successful
   authenticated outputs. Check denial for ordinary and signed-out users.
   The imported source-revision field describes the reviewed input checkpoint;
   it is not the later commit containing the generated output.
4. On resumption, the native onboarding flow must read this saved packet under
   the app's existing governance route, reconcile its exact app, pointer hash,
   observation references and later changes, and preserve still-valid history.
   Read current connection and source separately. A snapshot is not a fresh
   authentication, scan, entitlement grant or authorization to build.
5. Following each approved decision, intention or memory change, the existing
   governed writer must regenerate and review the snapshot from current source
   before updating its backend JSON under that approved work's scope. Missing
   or invalid source remains unavailable. Refreshing the page does not rewrite
   the capture date, grant approval or fill in missing evidence.

Native writer invocation, resumption integration, exact app plan approval and
live install/reload verification remain acceptance requirements. The local
preparer and backend are not an automatic live writer by themselves. Preserve
the immutable approved Governance Manifest and pending plan; adding this
separate display record never authorizes rehashing those files.

## Verification

`npm run test:base44-app-snapshot` covers the actual preparer and backend,
including a temporary Git repository, durable output reread, exact review hash,
source preservation, role changes, cross-app isolation, corrupt data, timeouts
and compile of the disabled Base44 entry. These are local checks, not a claim
that native Base44 has installed or exercised the backend.
